Genesis.author: Author uncertain; traditionally Moses; many scholars see later sources and editing
Genesis.authorNote: Genesis names no writer. Jewish and Christian tradition credits Moses with all five books of the Law: the Talmud says so (Bava Batra 14b), and the New Testament speaks of “the book of Moses” and “the law of Moses” (Mark 12:26; Luke 24:44, KJV). Many modern scholars, classically following Julius Wellhausen, see the five books as earlier sources (often labelled J, E, D and P) edited into a final form around the 6th–5th c. BC; that model is now much debated, and conservative scholars hold Moses to be the original author, with some later updating.

Deuteronomy.author: Author uncertain; traditionally Moses; many scholars tie its core to Josiah’s reform, c. 622 BC
